morning-rules.title: Do morning rules reduce my chances of an afternoon crash?
morning-rules.desc: 8-week exploration to see if early sunlight exposure, morning stretching, caffeine offsetting, or morning meditation help your afternoon energy.
startInstructions: Log your usual morning routine for the next few days to establish a baseline.
Each evening, record your afternoon energy level and any crash you notice.

outcomes.label: Morning sunlight: strong evidence for a shallower afternoon energy trough via circadian anchoring
Morning movement: moderate–strong evidence for sustained cognitive performance through the afternoon
Caffeine offsetting: moderate mechanistic evidence for reducing afternoon rebound crashes
Morning meditation: moderate evidence for lower afternoon fatigue via HRV and cortisol slope

phases.name: Weeks 1–2: Baseline
phases.desc: Log your usual morning routine and afternoon energy with no new rules — establish your personal baseline.

phases.name: Weeks 3–5: Morning rules
phases.desc: Track which rules you follow each day: sunlight, stretching, delayed caffeine, meditation.

phases.name: Weeks 6–7: Optimise your stack
phases.desc: Keep the rule combinations that helped most. Watch for fewer afternoon crashes.

phases.name: Week 8: Personalised trial analysis report
phases.desc: Your personal analysis of which morning rules linked to better afternoon energy for you.

eating.title: Does time restricted eating improve my energy levels?
eating.desc: 6-week exploration to see if a restriction in the time window in which you consume food helps to support higher energy levels through the day. No calorie restriction — just timing.
startInstructions: Log your natural eating times with no changes for the first two weeks.
Note your energy levels and hunger at key points through the day.

outcomes.label: Circadian alignment: strong evidence for more consistent energy across the day
Blood glucose stability: strong evidence for fewer afternoon energy dips
Sleep quality: moderate–strong evidence for higher baseline energy the next day
Mitochondrial efficiency: moderate evidence for higher-quality cellular energy output

phases.name: Weeks 1–2: Baseline eating window
phases.desc: Log your natural eating times with no changes.

phases.name: Weeks 3–4: 10-hour window
phases.desc: Compress eating to a consistent 10-hour window daily.

phases.name: Week 5: 8-hour window
phases.desc: Try an 8-hour window. Log energy and hunger response throughout.

phases.name: Week 6: Personalised trial analysis report
phases.desc: Your personal analysis of how meal timing affected your energy and hunger.

screen-sleep.title: Does moderation of screen exposure improve my sleep quality?
screen-sleep.desc: 6-week exploration to see if a reduction in screen exposure both before and at bedtime can increase sleep quality.
startInstructions: Log your normal evening screen habits and sleep quality for the baseline phase.
Each morning, rate how well you slept and note time to fall asleep.

outcomes.label: Blue light / melatonin: very strong evidence for faster sleep onset and better REM
Cognitive arousal: strong evidence for less fragmented, unrestored sleep
Circadian phase delay: strong evidence when evening screens shift sleep timing later
Sleep architecture: moderate–strong evidence for deeper, more restorative sleep

phases.name: Weeks 1–2: Baseline
phases.desc: Log your normal evening screen habits before bed, in-bed screen use, and sleep quality.

phases.name: Weeks 3–4: 30-min screen-free window
phases.desc: Stop all screens 30 min before bed and reduce in-bed screen use. Track sleep quality.

phases.name: Week 5: 60-min screen-free window
phases.desc: Extend to 60 min before bed and no screens in bed. Compare sleep quality across phases.

phases.name: Week 6: Personalised trial analysis report
phases.desc: Your personal analysis of how screen habits affected your sleep quality.

relaxation.title: Do relaxation practices improve my composure?
relaxation.desc: 6-week exploration to see if vagal breathing, progressive muscle relaxation, short (nature) walks, or meditation / visualisation help reduce stress and anxiety.
startInstructions: Log your stress levels and any relaxation practices you already use.
Note how composed you feel through the afternoon each day.

outcomes.label: Vagal breathing: strong evidence for rapid stress reduction within days
PMR: strong evidence for reduced trait anxiety over 4–8 weeks
Nature walks: strong evidence for lower rumination in single sessions
Meditation: very strong evidence for durable stress reactivity reduction

phases.name: Weeks 1–2: Baseline
phases.desc: Log your usual stress and anxiety with no new practices — establish your personal baseline.

phases.name: Weeks 3–5: Relaxation practices
phases.desc: Track which practices you follow each day: vagal breathing, PMR, short nature walks, meditation / visualisation.

phases.name: Week 6: Personalised trial analysis report
phases.desc: Your personal analysis of which practices linked to lower stress, anxiety, and greater composure for you.

upf-mood.title: Does reduction of Ultra Processed Food (UPF) improve my mood?
upf-mood.desc: 6-week exploration to see if a reduction in the daily intake of Ultra Processed Foods and their replacement with unprocessed foods can improve mood. Assess the percentage of your diet that day that contained UPF and track your daily mood and energy levels.
startInstructions: Log what you eat and how your mood feels through the day.
Track ultra-processed food intake alongside mood scores.

outcomes.label: Gut-brain axis: strong evidence for improved baseline mood via microbiome
Neuroinflammation: strong evidence linking lower UPF to reduced depressive symptoms
Blood glucose: strong evidence for less irritability and mood volatility
Nutrient displacement: moderate–strong evidence for better neurotransmitter support

phases.name: Weeks 1–2: Baseline
phases.desc: Log your usual share of UPF in meals plus daily mood and energy, with no intentional changes.

phases.name: Weeks 3–4: Gradual reduction
phases.desc: Replace key UPF items with unprocessed alternatives. Track UPF %, mood, and energy each day.

phases.name: Week 5: Sustained lower UPF
phases.desc: Hold a lower UPF target and compare mood and energy to your baseline weeks.

phases.name: Week 6: Personalised trial analysis report
phases.desc: Your personal analysis of how UPF reduction affected your mood and energy.
